solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A little mate who's spoilt

indicators.note: something spoilt has been ruined or messed up, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A slightly mocking remark about a friend who has been pampered and indulged.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat is an adverb of degree meaning to a small extent, just as a little qualifies an adjective or verb.

clue.text: Writer and Senior Common Room liable to fall out regularly

parts.note: SCR is the abbreviation for a university's Senior Common Room, the staff lounge

indicators.note: every other letter of liable drops out at regular intervals, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: A writer and the dons' common room who are prone to quarrelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall out' suggests an argument but means letters dropping out. The Senior Common Room is the lounge for fellows at Oxford and Cambridge colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is someone who writes, historically a copyist of manuscripts, and loosely any author.

clue.text: Better eat lime or bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go mad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Diet advice: it is better to eat limes or bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit on the menu but is the anagram signal; 'Better' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate or meliorate is to make something improve, which is to better it as a verb.

clue.text: Dreadfully important people celebrate capturing proverbial madman

parts.note: the world can mean people in general, as in all the world knows

indicators.note: the celebrating word takes the madman inside it, as a captor holds a prisoner

parts.note: to sing is to celebrate, as in sing the praises of
mad as a hatter is a proverbial phrase, so the hatter is the proverbial madman

explanation.surface: VIPs throwing a party after catching a notorious lunatic.
explanation.definitionFit: A world-shattering event is of enormous significance, momentous on a terrifying scale.

clue.text: Lover is tense, filled with misgivings at first

indicators.note: the grammatical tense has a letter put inside it, as a container is filled

parts.note: the aorist is a past tense in Greek grammar

indicators.note: only the first letter of misgivings is used

explanation.surface: A lover who is nervous and full of doubts at the start of an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like nervous but is the noun, a grammatical tense. The aorist is a Greek past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: An amorist is someone devoted to love or a lover, from Latin amor, love.

clue.text: Copulated like camels?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for had sex

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful pairing: one slang verb in the past tense and one adjective describing a camel's back.
explanation.definitionFit: Humped is both crude British slang for having sex and an adjective for an animal bearing a hump on its back.

clue.text: Can one rub Noel up the wrong way? Impossible to say

indicators.note: rubbing up the wrong way disturbs order, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether anyone could irritate a man named Noel; it's hard to tell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' belongs to the letters, not the idiom: the anagram uses Can one rub Noel up, with 'the wrong way' as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpronounceable cannot be spoken aloud correctly, so it is impossible to utter.

clue.text: Dad with interest in make-up

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
INT is the standard abbreviation for interest in finance

explanation.surface: A father taking an interest in cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint is an informal, slightly disparaging word for cosmetics applied to the face.

clue.text: Edit rag about international IT crowd

indicators.note: about signals moving letters around, so the letters of edit rag are rearranged

explanation.surface: Editing a tabloid about the international tech scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edit' looks like the signal for rearranging, but it is part of the letters with 'rag'; 'about' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: The digerati are people expert in digital technology, the computer-literate elite.

clue.text: Unlimited coffee, gin and weed ultimately cause upset

indicators.note: without its limits, its first and last letters, coffee keeps only its middle
ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of each of gin and weed

explanation.surface: Endless coffee, gin and dope will end up making trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend someone is to upset them or give displeasure, a verb meaning to cause hurt.

clue.text: Sovereign oddly ignored trouble with queen

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of trouble are dropped, leaving only its even-placed letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch who brushed aside difficulties alongside his consort.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign is a monarch, and a ruler is any person who governs a country or realm.

clue.text: Child leaving sprout

parts.note: to be off is to be leaving or departing
to spring is to sprout or grow up, as a plant springs from the ground

explanation.surface: A child departing home while a seedling shoots up: a picture of growing up and moving on.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's children or descendants, so one child is offspring.

clue.text: Diatribe is primarily baseless, by the way

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of baseless is taken

parts.note: something by the way, beside a road, is at the roadside

explanation.surface: A rant dismissed as groundless, mentioned as a casual aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' reads as a conversational aside but is taken literally: beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a fierce verbal attack, like a ship firing all guns on one side, so a diatribe.

clue.text: Animal that hides in earthenware vessels

indicators.note: the animal sits concealed within the word for earthenware, so the surrounding outer letters are stripped away

parts.note: pottery is a collective word for earthenware pots and vessels

explanation.surface: A creature tucked away inside clay pots, as a pet might curl up in a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal is not hidden in the clue's own letters: think of a synonym for earthenware vessels, POTTERY, and the animal sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a semi-aquatic mammal of rivers and coasts, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Court guards long for prestige

indicators.note: the court abbreviation surrounds the yearning word, as sentries enclose what they guard

parts.note: CT is the standard abbreviation for court, as in street names
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: Royal court guards yearning for social standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet means distinction or status in others' eyes, the same as prestige.

clue.text: Dryness of dead grass on golf course tee

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
the rough is the long grass bordering a golf fairway
T sounds like and is the shape of a tee; tee is the letter T spelt out

explanation.surface: Parched dead grass around a golf course tee during a dry spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a prolonged period without rain, that is a spell of dryness.

clue.text: Calculus annoys me after time

indicators.note: the word for me comes after the abbreviation for time

parts.note: to gall is to irritate or annoy
one is used for oneself, as in one does one's best, so it stands for me

explanation.surface: A maths student fed up with calculus after long hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calculus' suggests mathematics, but its older sense is a stone in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A calculus in medicine is a hard stone formed in the body, and a gallstone is one example.

clue.text: Pair of berks pursued by cool hitman

indicators.note: the pair of fools is chased by, so placed before, the cool word

parts.note: a berk is British slang for a fool, an ass, so two of them is ass twice
in means fashionable or cool

explanation.surface: Two idiots being chased by a calm contract killer.
explanation.walkthrough: A berk is a mildly rude British word for a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a hired killer who murders for money or politics, as a hitman does.

clue.text: One perspiring as we ate rancid sandwiches

indicators.note: the words as we ate rancid hold the answer between them, as bread holds a filling

explanation.surface: Someone sweating as a group eats sandwiches that have gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like the food being eaten but is the signal that the answer is held within the words.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sweats is literally a sweater, an agent noun from the verb to sweat.

clue.text: Right poetry books for Jerry or Roland?

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem, a piece of poetry
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Choosing the right poetry books for two people called Jerry and Roland.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerry is the mouse in Tom and Jerry; Roland Rat was a puppet star of British TV in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerry is a cartoon mouse and Roland a puppet rat, both examples of the gnawing mammal family, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Snarl and bite leg but not tail

parts.note: a sharp bite or zest in flavour is a tang

indicators.note: the word leg is used without its final letter, its tail

explanation.surface: A dog growling and nipping someone's leg, but sparing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snarl' suggests the dog's growl, but here it means a knot or muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A snarl is a knotted mass of hair or string, which is a tangle.

clue.text: Part of mosaic in potentate's seraglio

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words potentate's seraglio, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A mosaic decorating a sultan's harem.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small square tiles of stone or glass from which a mosaic is assembled.

clue.text: Heartily herding relative's cows

indicators.note: heartily points to the heart of herding, its central letter

parts.note: aunt's, possessive of aunt, a relative

explanation.surface: Enthusiastically rounding up a relative's cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cows' looks like cattle in a herd, but it is the verb meaning intimidates.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, and to daunt is likewise to frighten or dishearten.

clue.text: Broadcast key passage

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard on air, so the word is chosen for how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a key, or cay, is a low island, an isle

explanation.surface: A radio broadcast of a key passage of music or text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is the low coral island, as in the Florida Keys, not a key on a keyboard or lock.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats or shelves, so a passage.

clue.text: Power of vacuous sci-fi novel

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so sci-fi is emptied of its inside, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: The strength of a brainless science-fiction book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book but is the adjective meaning fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew means muscular strength or vigour, as in the sinews of war, so power.

clue.text: Indigestion from hectic days drinking cola

indicators.note: the jumbled days take in the cola, as a drinker takes in a drink
hectic means frantic and disordered, so the letters of days are mixed up

parts.note: Pepsi is a brand of cola

explanation.surface: Stomach trouble after frantic days spent guzzling fizzy cola.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' is the container signal: the scrambled days take the cola brand inside them, the way a drinker swallows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is the medical term for indigestion, discomfort from poor digestion.

clue.text: Feeling one's constrained by life, perhaps

indicators.note: the letter for one is held in by the prison term, as a prisoner is confined

parts.note: a life term is an example of a prison sentence, hence perhaps
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is one is, linking to the indicator

explanation.surface: Someone feeling hemmed in by the way their life has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life' is not existence but a life sentence in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel or perceive, so feeling in the noun sense.

clue.text: Admit being to the right of British ex-PM

indicators.note: in an across answer, what lies to the right comes after, so the admitting word follows the British abbreviation

parts.note: to own up, or own, is to admit

explanation.surface: Confessing to being further right than a former British Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British' looks like part of the definition but supplies BR. Gordon Brown was UK Labour Prime Minister from 2007 to 2010.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordon Brown was Britain's Prime Minister from 2007 to 2010, so a former premier.

clue.text: Refuse initially to change direction, like some travellers

indicators.note: the opening letter, a compass point, is switched to another compass point

parts.note: sewage is waste matter, refuse
S is the compass abbreviation for south
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Travellers initially refusing to alter their route.
explanation.walkthrough: S for south at the start of SEWAGE becomes N for north. New Age travellers are British itinerant groups living in vans and buses.
explanation.definitionFit: New Age travellers are a British countercultural movement of nomadic people living in vehicles, so some travellers are described as new-age.

clue.text: Ever-fashionable daughter dieted

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
someone who dieted ate less

explanation.surface: A stylish daughter who went on a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dateless never goes out of style, being timeless and always in fashion.
